title: RunCycleFromPhase's shared cycleRun re-seats different field subsets at three sites — extract one seat helper
summary: resume.go now hoists ONE cycleRun (timingOwner) so the phase-timing composition happens exactly once across the abnormal-epilogue defer, the timing defer and the completion path. Correct today, but the three sites re-seat DIFFERENT subsets of its fields (construction; cs/state/result; cs/phaseTimings; ctx/cs/state/result/phaseTimings/preCycleHEAD), so verifying it means checking per site that it seats everything its callee reads.
root_cause: A shared mutable struct with implicit per-site field requirements. Adding a field that abnormalEpilogue reads means remembering to seat it at every site; the failure mode is a stale cs.WorkspacePath writing the timing log into the wrong workspace.
fix: Extract one `func (cr *cycleRun) seat(...)` (or a small per-consumer accessor) so each site states its intent once, or at minimum a comment at the hoist naming which fields each consumer reads.
acceptance: Each of the three resume.go sites seats through one named helper rather than an ad-hoc field list.
A new field consumed by abnormalEpilogue cannot be silently unseated at one site — demonstrated by the helper's signature or by a test.
Resume normal/abort/zero-entry paths keep today's behavior; internal/core -race green.
connects_to: the 2026-09-11 dossier-evidence projection fix, which introduced the shared owner
notes: Architecture reviewer MEDIUM, round 3, explicitly a follow-up rather than a merge condition. The end-to-end guard the same review asked for (a test driving RunCycleFromPhase) landed partially as core/phase_timing_single_writer_test.go, a source-scan guard pinning the writer count at 1.
